corrected_verdict: PARTIALLY_KNOWN (stronger than the checker said): the nu=3 case (n=2) of the block is in ML prior art. Tian arXiv 2410.01779 (NeurIPS 2025) gives the 3-node cube-root-of-unity per-frequency block, proves that order-1 and order-2 cannot cancel the sign-flipped terms (App. Lemma 5), and derives equal amplitudes and phases 2pi/3, 4pi/3 as the minimal-L2-norm order-3 solution (App. Lemma 6, Eqs. 91-96). The general-nu identity is Mohlenkamp-Monzon Thm 2. New: general nu, the L_{2,b} norm accounting, lambda_j^nu proportional to y*_j, and attaining Gamma_s.
issues: MISSED PRIOR ART: Tian, 'Composing Global Solutions to Reasoning Tasks via Algebraic Objects in Neural Nets' (arXiv 2410.01779v4, NeurIPS 2025). In a quadratic-activation MSE network the cross term (w_a.e_a)(w_b.e_b)w_c is a degree-3 product neuron. Tian's Table 1 generator u_syn=[w3,w3,w3] gives rho(u_syn)=u^2+u+1, i.e. 3 hidden nodes per frequency with cube-root-of-unity phases, and this kills every sign-flipped sum potential. Fig. 2 (bottom) shows gradient descent finding exactly this 3-node block when the R* term is dropped. App. Lemma 5 shows every order-1/2 solution satisfying R_c has r_kkk=0, so 3 nodes are necessary. App. Lemma 6 and Eqs. 91-96 show the min-norm order-3 solution is equal magnitude with phases 0, 2pi/3, 4pi/3 (up to signs +-1). So the checker's sentence 'None of the ML constructions uses a nu-neuron roots-of-unity block' is false at nu=3. The paper must cite Tian at prop:block and also at lem:cost as the nu=3 count case. The r12-cost-of-feature verifier's statement that Tian 'proves no lower bound and no norm cost' is inaccurate for the same reason. Tian stops at n=2, uses MSE rather than max-margin, and uses equal amplitudes over all frequencies, so general nu, the lambda_j^nu proportional to y*_j weighting and attaining Gamma_s remain new. CONFIRMED CITATIONS all re-checked and correct: Mohlenkamp-Monzon (Crossref Math. Intelligencer 27(2):65-69, 2005; Thm 2, the 'separation rank n' sentence and Fig. 1 alpha=0,pi/3,2pi/3 read in the preprint); Morwani App. F.2 '8 neurons for each of the frequencies'; Li et al. Lemma E.3 2^{2k-1} per frequency (abstract and Thm 4.1 widths use 2^{2k-2}(p-1)); Gromov random uniform phases; He et al. Def 4.1 iota in {2,4} and Prop 4.2. Numerical check: prop:block's table identity holds exactly as written for n=1..6. Other candidates checked and not prior art: Huang-Li 2511.23443 (width-2 sine nets), Tian 2509.21519. TOOLING (explains the slow verify stage): WebSearch refuses with a '200 of 200' session budget, shared across all workflow agents. Verifiers must fall back to curl on arXiv PDFs and the API, Crossref and OpenAlex, and some of those return 429 rate limits.

extra_citations.why: nu=3 precedent for prop:block and lem:cost. The 3-node cube-root-of-unity per-frequency block rho(u_syn) (Table 1, Fig. 2 bottom) cancels all sign-flipped terms. App. Lemma 5 shows fewer than 3 nodes cannot do this, and App. Lemma 6 / Eqs. 91-96 give equal amplitudes with phases 2pi/3, 4pi/3 as the min-norm order-3 solution. The setting is quadratic activation with MSE loss and n=2 only.
